audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart shows Skill on rows 3-4 and Ryze on rows 5-6 while its own whys, the content win[] and the packet chart all give Mel every stage.
audit.why: Kit supports Mel: her Q is 950 range vs his 615 W/E combo range, Rebuttal reflects his Q and E projectiles, and Realm Warp is a map tool not a duel button. Full sides on 5-6 sat over whys describing Mel winning — the sides were the defect.
audit.corrected: Sides aligned to Mel; see edits.

audit.why: Spikes covered correctly: his 3-5 combo window, Realm Warp 6 as roam tool, his Tear/Archangel first-item spike, his late sustained DPS. All 4 spikes present and kit-consistent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldowns field had no digits; Rune Prison being targeted (root lands through Rebuttal's projectile reflect, only damage blanked) was unstated; Do's/Don'ts bodies were pasted trade strings.
audit.why: Kit: his Q 5s / 1000 range projectile, W 11s / 615 targeted root, E 3.5s / 615 projectile, R 180s. Mel W 38-26s. Q and E carry the projectile flag; W does not.
50.5% over 903 games; EVEN 5.5/10 and an all-Mel lane chart with his scaling threat noted is coherent.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Q-volley the last-hit from 950 — his combo needs 615 range and a flux mark, so the chip is free while you stand clean.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Burning Rebuttal on a lone 5s Q and then eating the flux-root combo it existed to return — spend the reflect on the EQ chain.

edits.before: Ryze wins by landing Rune Prison (Root), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Ryze wins by tagging you with Flux, chaining Rune Prison into Overload spam, and scaling free if you let him farm.

edits.before: Good trade: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages. Bad trade: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Good trade: Q-volley the last-hit from 950 — his combo needs 615 range and a flux mark, so the chip is free while you stand clean. Bad trade: Burning Rebuttal on a lone 5s Q and then eating the flux-root combo it existed to return — spend the reflect on the EQ chain.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): matchup-defining — Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Check it before every step-up. - W Rebuttal is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Rune Prison is 11s and only 615 range — outside it his root doesn't exist; that's your spacing rule. - His 5s Q is a projectile: Rebuttal (38s) reflects it and breaks the EQ chain. - Flux comes every 3.5s; never idle beside a marked minion.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Fire the volley right after his E-flux lands on the wave — his root needs 615 range, yours lands from 950, so the window is free.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Q and E are projectiles Rebuttal returns, but Rune Prison is targeted — the root lands through the glow, only its damage is blanked.
